standards.scope: Combined frozen repair source, documentation and attributed salvage evidence; execution, sweep, legacy push and identity regressions executed from extracted frozen sources.
standards.qualification_note: An initial identity test selector used the wrong class name; corrected selectors were freshly rerun successfully.

spec.scope: Combined frozen repair against the approved SPEC, 18 tickets and six branch-review findings; independently executed material public CLI scenarios.

resolved_findings: Abandonment, GC and destructive sweep acquire the check execution lock.
Legacy Git children inherit both landing locks; uncertain pushes remain fenced without affirmative exact-ref rejection evidence.
Check receipts require process-group quiescence after timeout and after a successful leader exit.
Bookkeeping commits validate and retain the original repository identity before publication.
Corenius abandonment releases the exact owned claim through a committed tracker transition with recoverable before and after hashes.
Dirty cleanup revalidates current ownership, liveness, locks, source bytes and recovery archives before clearing files.
limitations: Reviewers did not repeat the broad repository gate.
Salvage cleanup qualification is separately attributed in salvage-cleanup.json.
Changed claims or ticket bytes require explicit reconciliation; automatic release preserves them.
